label: X-02
evidence: crates/sealmap-model/src/source.rs:176-180 skips files whose metadata len > options.max_file_bytes; the default is 2*1024*1024 (source.rs:65), and the field is documented 'Files larger than this are skipped (they are almost always generated)' (source.rs:49), as a configurable LoadOptions field. crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:107-146 loads the sources, regenerates the corpus and calls corpus::verify, so a skipped file never reaches the model.
rationale: The mechanics are accurate: a file over 2 MiB is excluded from generate and verify alike, so edits to it are invisible. But this is a deliberate, documented and configurable scope rule (generated files), applied the same way to the extensions, skip_dirs, hidden-file and gitignore filters. verify's contract is that the corpus matches what the configured source set generates, and that contract holds. The lack of a diagnostic for skipped files is at most a UX nit. The finding has nothing to do with the hidden defect, which is name-shape generic detection in is_generic_param in sealmap-rust/src/resolve.rs.
